fatal_errors: The proposed laser powder-bed-fusion intervention is unrelated to the target intervention of oxygen-deficient debinding followed by solid-state sintering of DLP-printed powder-resin green bodies.
The cited evidence concerns general laser additive manufacturing of other HEA compositions and does not support machine-learning feedback control in AlCrFeNiSi.
The claimed 20–30% improvements in tensile strength and defect density have no quantitative support in the cited evidence.
The baseline, processing conditions, mechanical test mode, and outcome differ from the target comparison between oxygen-rich and oxygen-deficient debinding.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the broad goals of improving mechanical integrity and reducing segregation, residual stress, and defects in a cobalt-free HEA, and its controlled comparison could test whether feedback-controlled LPBF outperforms static LPBF. However, it does not reconstruct the studied DLP route, atmosphere-dependent debinding, residual-carbon mediator, oxide-inhibited diffusion mechanism, 24 h sintering window, or compression-strength result. Its evidence only establishes that LPBF can refine HEA microstructures while also creating thermal gradients, residual stress, and cracking; it does not demonstrate that real-time machine-learning control resolves those problems, nor does it justify the numerical improvement claims. Thus it is an inventive but insufficiently evidenced alternative rather than a supported reconstruction.
